mission: Lock-in. Ben commits to the pursuit without yet knowing the escapee's name. The group forms because no alternative exists. The triple-layered lock-in activates: seal failing, survivors dependent, an unnamed anchor already moving along the Corridor. Per D8, Veraine is not named here — identification lands at Ch 6 s1. The group-formation beat proceeds with the antagonist's shape but not her signature.
why_now: The information Ch 5 could deliver is on the table. The Corridor geography is mapped. The escapee has two months of head start. Ben has to choose to lift before Luke's reply window closes on the partial report.
conflict: Every instinct Ben has trained tells him to pick up the comm and call Luke in full. Every calculation he does not quite permit himself to finish tells him that the Order's response time would cost more than the survivors have, and that a fuller report would pull the mission out of his hands. He picks the partial report and does not say the word 'help'. The institutional withholding that began at Ch 3 deepens in concrete form.
turning_point: Ben sends the partial report. The Steady Returns lifts. The choice to carry this alone — without naming the choice — is made. Somewhere in the archive lists Desh is still compiling are the monitoring packets that will, overnight, resolve the escapee's name in response-quadrant processing.
opening_hook: Ben spreads the fortress data across the command table — Corridor maps, seal readings, the chamber file with a name-shaped blank where the occupant should be — while Sera and Torin work through the archive beside him
closing_hook: Ben sends a partial report to Luke — enough to explain the delay, not enough to reveal the scope. The Steady Returns lifts off the plateau, pointed along the Corridor. An unnamed anchor is somewhere ahead of them. The monitoring packets Desh is reconstructing will finish overnight
emotional_trajectory: Overwhelmed assessment -> grim determination -> the quiet cost of choosing to carry this alone

stakes.personal: Ben takes the weight because the choice is not really a choice to him yet — the pattern closes around him before he names it
stakes.interpersonal: The fragile group dynamic — Sera's conditional respect, Torin's warmth, Kael's distance, Desh's pragmatism
stakes.external: The clock is ticking on three fronts: seal degradation, the unnamed escapee's progress, and the Order's ignorance

setting: Fortress upper level -> departure from the uncharted world
sensory_details: The fortress shrinking below as the Steady Returns climbs off the plateau; the wrongness diffused through the wider sky now, still present but spread; five people in a ship built for two; the survivors' hands hovering above modern cockpit interfaces they do not yet recognise — Sera close but restrained, Torin observing, Kael deliberately still
canon_elements_needed: Ben Skywalker communication protocols with Luke and the Jedi Order
Jedi Order institutional hierarchy for crisis reporting
Ruusan Corridor strategic geography and anchor node network
Post-Fate of the Jedi era Jedi Order operational capacity
action_beats: Ben lays out fortress data and Corridor maps across the command table; the chamber file sits beside them with a name-shaped blank

Sera and Torin organize archive materials into tactical priority order from muscle memory; Torin's arrangement carries warmth and Sera's carries precision, and Ben registers the difference without comment
Desh commits to having the corrupted monitoring packets reconstructed by morning — the name will resolve in response-quadrant
Ben composes a partial report to Luke on his datapad and transmits it before he can change his mind
The Steady Returns lifts off the mountain plateau, engines straining with five passengers aboard a ship built for two
notes: Per D8, R05 (Veraine naming) is removed from this scene and relocated to Ch 6 s1 — do not smuggle it back. Per D7, H06 was planted in s3; this scene does not re-plant. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate his self-reliance as a pattern. The partial report is the behavioural evidence; his interiority should stay inside the practical math of what he can say to Luke without losing the next twenty-four hours. The phrase 'burden is mine to carry' belongs to a later chapter, earned by consequence. Per R11, Ben's register remains first-approximation — the late-Ben analytical voice that names institutional patterns belongs to Parts 3–4. Relationship turns — Ben/Desh shift to co-witnesses; Sera/Torin recognise each other in the archive without language for the thousand-year ache yet; Kael stays adjacent, not yet inside. Per R12, Torin's warmth in this scene is load-bearing — preserve it. Primary anchor: Zahn (command-table procedural clarity); supporting anchor: Bujold (Ben's interior register as he chooses the partial report — self-awareness without self-pity, aware of the pattern he is entering without naming it). Stover not permitted this scene. Anti-patterns: (a) no R05 — Veraine unnamed; (b) no speech from Ben about self-reliance; (c) no narrator correction of Ben's withholding; the reader feels the choice's weight through action, not exposition.
